questions.explain: The chapter states proposals with confidence >= 0.70 are auto-apply candidates, 0.40-0.70 require async human review, and below 0.40 are suppressed.
options: Scores >= 0.70 are auto-apply candidates; 0.40-0.70 require async human review; below 0.40 are suppressed
Scores >= 0.90 auto-apply; everything else is dropped
Any score above 0.50 auto-applies immediately
Scores determine naming only; all proposals need human approval
questions.q: What are the confidence-score thresholds in the index proposal scoring model, and what does each mean?

questions.explain: SQL Server's CREATE INDEX WITH (ONLINE = ON) builds while holding only brief locks at start and end; on Standard Edition online operations are unavailable, so the apply layer falls back to an offline build inside a maintenance window.
options: Use MAXDOP = 1 and rebuild offline during business hours
Drop and recreate the index to avoid sort overhead
Increase the index fill factor to 100
Use CREATE INDEX ... WITH (ONLINE = ON), checking edition support and falling back to an offline build in a maintenance window when online is unavailable
questions.q: How does the chapter's autonomous apply layer create indexes safely under live traffic?

questions.explain: The retirement pipeline: observation (zero reads 14+ days across three stat-reset cycles), DISABLE (reversible, drops pages but keeps metadata), 24h disable testing, DROP, then post-drop monitoring with a suppression record.
options: Observation -> Disable -> 24h testing -> Drop -> post-drop monitoring with a suppression record
Immediate DROP without testing
Rebuild the index first, then drop it
Archive the index to a history table
questions.q: What is the graduated state machine for retiring an unused index?

questions.explain: The chapter notes SQL Server has no supported documented mechanism for hypothetical indexes (AUTOPILOT is undocumented and not production-safe); teams rely on missing-index DMV cost/impact estimates, refreshed column statistics, and real builds in staging or low-traffic windows for validation.
options: The chapter recommends AUTOPILOT as fully production-safe
Use the Database Engine Tuning Advisor's inline API
SQL Server has no supported documented hypothetical-index mechanism, so teams rely on missing-index DMV estimates, updated column statistics, and real builds in staging or low-traffic windows
Hypothetical indexes are built directly in production
questions.q: How does the chapter recommend validating an index candidate on SQL Server before creating it in production?

questions.explain: Expand/contract: add the new column with dual-write trigger, backfill in batches, update application bindings, then swap/drop — and phase 3 (removal) always requires human sign-off regardless of score.
options: Rewrite the entire table with the new type in a single transaction
Add a new column with dual-write trigger, backfill in batches, update application bindings, then swap/drop — with the removal phase always requiring human sign-off
Update the column type directly with ALTER COLUMN during peak hours
Export data, drop the table, recreate with the new type, reload
questions.q: What migration pattern does the chapter prescribe for autonomous column type evolution, and what is its governance constraint?
